tools.name: search_cards
tools.description: Filter the US credit-card dataset by product type, rewards currency (program name or kind), issuer, annual fee, foreign-transaction fee, signup-bonus value, credit band, or curated category. Searches ONLY issuer-verified cards by default, because unverified stubs carry null for most filterable field

tools.name: get_card
tools.description: Full detail for a single card by id (slug), including earn rates, credits, eligibility, sources and lastVerified. The apply link is our tracked redirect, not the issuer URL.

tools.name: estimate_rewards
tools.description: Given an annual spending profile (USD per category, e.g. { dining: 6000, groceries: 8000, travel: 4000, other: 20000 }), estimate each card's net rewards value and rank them. Net value = rewards earned on spend + first-year signup bonus − annual fee. Statement credits are reported separately (max va

tools.name: check_eligibility
tools.description: Given a user's credit band (and optionally income), return cards they would typically qualify for, surfacing issuer application rules (e.g. Chase 5/24) and any income floor. Only cards that publish a credit requirement can be answered; cards with no published requirement are counted in `unknownCount

tools.name: get_apply_link
tools.description: Return the apply link for a card. This is always a creditcards.best tracked redirect that records the referral and forwards to the issuer; the raw issuer URL is never returned.

tools.name: compare_cards
tools.description: Side-by-side detail for two or more cards by id: fees, foreign-transaction fee, signup bonus, earn rates, credits and eligibility. Apply links are tracked redirects.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_apply_link" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.creditcards.best" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_card, get_apply_link · Private data: get_apply_link · Public sink: check_eligibility.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_card, get_apply_link · Private data: get_apply_link · Public sink: check_eligibility

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
